Q: How to check a `struct gps_data_t*` for a NULL value the safe way? A:

Some [side] notes:

  1. It is better to avoid raw new (and delete).
    You can use a smart pointer instead that will manage the memory automatically:
    std::unique_ptr by default or std::shared_ptr if you need shared ownership.
    In many cases you can even avoid any kind of pointer and use the type directly.

  2. It is better to separate assignment (response = ...) from checking the result.
    This will make the code clearer and can also help with debugging while stepping through.

Q: Remove/undef a class method A:

You can remove a method in two easy ways. The drastic

Module#undef_method( )

removes all methods, including the inherited ones. The kinder

Module#remove_method( )

removes the method from the receiver, but it leaves inherited methods alone.

See below 2 simple example -

Example 1 using undef_method

class A 
    def x
        puts "x from A class"
    end
end

class B < A
    def x
        puts "x from B Class"
    end
    undef_method :x
end

obj = B.new
obj.x
# undefined method `x' for an instance of B (NoMethodError)

Example 2 using remove_method

class A 
    def x
        puts "x from A class"
    end
end

class B < A
    def x
        puts "x from B Class"
    end
    remove_method :x
end

obj = B.new
obj.x
# x from A class

Q: SQL SUM function not summing A:

The result rows with all zeros should stem from non-exercise rows. Rows with a sum, but a zero count, however, should not be possible with the code you are showing. That you don't get one result row per person, is because in your GROUP BY clause you ask explicitly for one result row per person and event.

Solution: Just filter the joined rows right away and group by person. You'll want to outer join this to the persons table, if you want to include persons without any matching data, or inner join it otherwise.

SELECT 
  p.person_name,
  COALESCE(x.gr_pct, 0) AS growth_percent,
  COALESCE(x.gr_cnt, 0) AS growth_count,
  COALESCE(x.co_pct, 0) AS composite_percent,
  COALESCE(x.co_cnt, 0) AS composite_count
FROM datawarehouse.dtbl_persons p
LEFT JOIN
(
  SELECT
    en.person_key,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Growth' THEN en.event_percentile END) AS gr_pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Growth' THEN 1 END) AS gr_cnt,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Composite' THEN en.event_percentile END) AS co_pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Composite' THEN 1 END) AS co_cnt
  FROM datawarehouse.ftbl_event_norms en
  JOIN datawarehouse.dtbl_events e ON e.events_key = en.events_key
  WHERE e.event_company = 'exercise'
    AND e.event_topic = 'quantitative'
    AND e.event_level IN ('Composite', 'Growth')
  GROUP BY en.person_key
 ) x ON x.person_key = p.person_key
ORDER BY p.person_name;

Q: Should I change RSA algorithm to some more modern algorithm or just stay on RSA but use larger key length? A:

If RSA-6144 is too slow, don't switch to larger RSA. I would generally suggest for future improvement using ECDSA for authentication. If you need forward secrecy for sessions, use ECDHE, usually X25519 or P-256 for key exchange. These options are generally faster than large RSA and achieve comparable security with much smaller key sizes.

Keep in mind these options are not PQ-Safe- if you need post-quantum key establishment, look at ML-KEM.

Q: Making Maven run all tests, even when some fail A:

* -fae + -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false -- skips affected modules + output "BUILD FAILURE" + error exit status

* -fae + -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true -- runs all modules + output "BUILD SUCCESS" + exit status 0 (success) despite test failure

* -fn + -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false -- runs all modules + output "BUILD FAILURE" + exit status 0 (success) despite test failure

To run all tests even when some fail (in a module on which other modules depend) - and set the exit status - I'm evaluating mvn -fn -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=false ... | grep -c "BUILD SUCCESS" (which can be combined with tee).
